Chapter 8
Contract and Scheduling Agreement
Management
Purchase contracts and scheduling agreements are agreements made by
a buying organization with a supplier for materials and services over a
specified period of time. These long-term arrangements are often the
result of supplier negotiations and are often linked to legal contract doc-
uments. This chapter describes the process of managing and monitoring
these documents, including creation, execution, monitoring analysis,
and renewal in SAP S/4HANA.
This chapter explains the processes used to manage outline agreements in SAP S/4HANA.
Outline agreements are documents used to manage delivery of goods or services from a
supplier over a specified period of time. Outline agreements in SAP S/4HANA come in two
forms: contracts and scheduling agreements. The properties and apps used to manage
and analyze these documents are described in the sections ahead. We’ve also provided
the detailed configuration steps required in SAP S/4HANA to set up contracts and sched-
uling agreements based on your enterprise’s requirements.
Businesses are becoming increasingly competitive and success-driven in today’s digi-
tal economy. To be a successful organization, it’s essential that the procurement pro-
cess, which is one of the core lines of business for any industry, is run with high
efficiency and low costs. Most companies use the concept of longer-term purchasing
agreements with suppliers to achieve procurement process optimization and
improved financial performance. Such agreements are defined as outline purchase
agreements, which may be referred to as blanket or umbrella agreements outside SAP
systems. Outline purchase agreements in SAP S/4HANA consist of contracts, centrally
agreed upon contracts, distributed contracts, scheduling agreements, and scheduling
agreements referencing a centrally agreed upon contract. The solution addressing
these agreements is referred to as purchase contract management under the sourcing
and contract management stream in SAP S/4HANA, as shown in Figure 8.1.

8.1 What Is Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management?
Contract and scheduling agreement management within SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and
Procurement refers to the management of long-term purchasing arrangements with
suppliers for supply of materials or performance of services. Purchases made with ref-
erence to these documents help streamline the procurement process. Well-designed
contracts and scheduling agreements can help reduce prices and guarantee on-time
supply, which helps plan and optimize the business processes of both the purchasing
organization and the supplying organization. The analytics capabilities and innova-
tions offered by SAP S/4HANA enable procurement processes that are in real time and
efficient.
A purchase contract is a document created and maintained in the SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem. This document holds all the information relevant to the agreement between the
purchasing organization and the supplier. Once the quantities, prices, terms, and con-
ditions are finalized, the purchase contract is created in the system. The different types
of contracts and how they’re created in the system are explained in this section.
8.1.1 Types of Purchase Contracts
A purchase contract is a type of supplier outline agreement in SAP S/4HANA that allows
for the issue of release orders (a.k.a., call-off orders) for the agreed-upon materials or
services of the contract over the life of the document. A contract is suitable when a
long-term agreement with a supplier is in place but the demand for the goods or ser-
vices cannot be pinned to a predictable schedule. This means that release purchase
orders are created, either manually or via materials planning, when they are needed to
fulfill sales or production demands. These purchase contracts in SAP S/4HANA consist
of items, which are materials, material groups, or services. It’s possible to create the fol-
lowing types of contracts, depending on the business requirements:

 Quantity contract
This type of contract stipulates the quantity, negotiated price, and conditions for
purchase of materials or services from the supplier with whom the contract is estab-
lished. This allows the purchaser to issue multiple release orders to the supplier with
reference to the contract until the total released quantity reaches the target quantity
defined in the contract.
 Value contract
These contracts are generally used for purchasing materials or services that belong
to certain material groups defined in materials management. These contracts stipu-
late the total value of the contract—which is also known as the target value—and of
the material groups and the supplier. Specific materials or services are not listed as
line items in the contract, but the contract allows purchase of materials or services
that belong to the material groups that are listed as line items in the contract. Pur-
chasers can create release orders for materials or services that belong to the material
groups identified in the contract. This allows the purchaser to issue multiple release
orders to the supplier with reference to the contract until the total released value
reaches the target value defined in the contract.
 Contract release order
It’s possible to create a release order, which is simply a purchase order referencing a
contract, using SAP GUI Transaction ME21N. In this transaction, if you enter the con-
tract number in the Outline Agreement field under the Items pane, the system will
populate all the information from the contract and expect you to input the quantity
and delivery date. After creating the release order, it’s possible to edit and display the
document using Transactions ME22N and ME23N. With the introduction of SAP Fiori
apps in SAP S/4HANA, the UI has moved away from the old SAP GUI–based transac-
tions to the new SAP Fiori UX, which is explained in the next section.
8.1.2 Manage Purchase Contracts
The Manage Purchase Contracts app is used for creating and editing purchase contract
documents. These documents can be created either directly by entering all the data
manually or by referencing purchase requisitions, RFQs/quotations, or existing con-
tracts. With the introduction of SAP Fiori apps for SAP S/4HANA, the Manage Purchase
Contracts app is used for creating or editing contracts, as follows:
1. Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad and click the Manage Purchase Contracts tile to
open the app.
2. Click the Create button to create a contract. The header screen, shown in Figure 8.2,
is presented for entering header information.

8.2 Contract Consumption
Purchasing managers and buyers want to monitor existing contracts in the system and
analyze consumption patterns. They also want to obtain advance information about
both planned and predicted expiry dates of contracts. This information helps the pur-
chasing organization regulate consumption and initiate contract renewal or the rene-
gotiation process. This section describes the SAP Fiori apps available in SAP S/4HANA
to both analyze and predict contract data.
8.2.1 Value Contract Consumption
The Value Contract Consumption SAP Fiori app analyses the value contracts in the sys-
tem and displays target and released amounts and the consumption percentage over
the last 365 days. Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad and navigate to the Value Contract
Consumption app, then click the tile to execute the app. It’s possible to display the met-
rics by supplier, purchasing group, purchasing organization, document, and trend, as
shown in Figure 8.11. The output can be filtered by Purchase Contract, Document Type,
Supplier, Calendar Week/Month/Quarter/Year, Purchasing Group/Organization, Sup-
plier, Currency, Company Code, and Created By, as shown in Figure 8.11 1.
Note that the columns represent Released Amount, Target Amount, and Consumption % 2.
Figure 8.11 Value Contract Consumption
From the initial display—for example, By Supplier—it’s possible to drill down by click-
ing on any bar (representing one supplier’s data) and selecting one of the options, as
shown in Figure 8.12, to go to the next level. Once you choose, for example, Purchasing
Group from the options, you’ll see the values for the selected supplier per purchasing
group.

8.3 Contract Reporting and Analytics
Reporting and analytics in contract management have undergone major changes in SAP
S/4HANA. The capability that comes with the in-memory technology of SAP S/4HANA
and the SAP Fiori UX has made it possible to offer new innovations in the areas of
reporting and analytics. This section provides information for all contract management
SAP Fiori apps for reporting and analytics that come standard with SAP S/4HANA.
8.3.1 Unused Contracts
The Unused Contracts app identifies all purchase contracts that haven’t been used
within the last 365 days from the current date. These contracts are listed along with the
target and released amounts (see Figure 8.15). The output can be displayed by supplier,
purchasing group, purchasing organization, purchasing document category, or docu-
ment in tabular format or as a chart. You can drill down to view the related documents
by clicking any of the bars in the bar chart view and selecting the Documents naviga-
tion option.
Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Unused Contracts app, and click its
tile to execute the app. This app provides insight into unused contracts and enables the
buyer to analyze and take necessary action to better utilize the contract.
In Figure 8.15 1, you can filter by purchase contract, calendar year, purchasing group/
organization, supplier, currency, company code, and document creator. You may select
By Supplier to search by supplier, by purchasing group or organization, or document 2.
Note that the columns represent Target Amount, Released Amount, and Unused Con-
tracts 3.

8.3.2 Off-Contract Spend
Often, purchases are made without using a negotiated price for materials or services.
This may be because no negotiated price exists or because there is ignorance that a
contract exists for that material or service. Procurement managers always want to
know how much or what percentage of materials are procured outside of negotiated
contracts. Analyzing this information helps buyers determine the types of products
and areas in need of further contracts and negotiated prices. The Off-Contract Spend
app (see Figure 8.16) enables the buyer to analyze and control such purchases, resulting
in improved procurement processes and reduced costs.
Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Off-Contract Spend app, and click its
tile to execute the app. In this app, the total amount of purchase order items without
any contract reference is expressed as a percentage of the total amount of all the pur-
chase order items over a period of one year from the previous year to date. The app
shows both the off-contract spend amount and the spend percentage.
In Figure 8.16 1, you can filter by calendar week/month/quarter/year, company code,
supplier, supplier country, material, plant, purchasing group/organization, material
group, purchasing category, purchasing order, currency, and document creator. You may
select By Supplier to search by supplier, by purchasing category or material group, by pur-
chasing group or organization, plant, cost center or WBS element, document, or trend 2.
Note that the columns represent Off Contr. Spend Amt and Off Contract Spend % 3.
Figure 8.16 Off-Contract Spend
The values can be displayed by supplier, purchasing group, purchasing organization, pur-
chasing category, or material group, plant, WBS element, cost center, and trend in tabular
format or as a chart. The app can display all documents that contribute to the spend. It’s
also possible to analyze the trend of the spend by purchasing category or by supplier.

ument in this app by clicking any of the bars in the bar chart view and selecting the

8.4 Configuration
To realize the features and functionalities of contract management, the system needs
to be configured based on business requirements. This section provides the details of
standard SAP-recommended configuration steps for contract management. These set-
tings are made in the SAP S/4HANA system by following the customizing paths pro-
vided in the following sections for each step.
8.4.1 Configuring Contracts
With SAP S/4HANA, it’s possible to take advantage of the SAP Best Practices activation
approach for customizing, as explained in Chapter 2. However, if you use the tradi-
tional customizing approach, this section can help. This information also helps validate
the SAP standard configuration.
Define Document Types
Contracts are managed in the system as documents. Document types, which act as a key
to group contracts, are defined in configuration. To define document types, navigate to
IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Purchasing  Contract  Define Document Types.

document types depending on business requirements. Number ranges are assigned to

used as required. The menu path to set number ranges is IMG (SPRO)  Materials Manage-
ment  Purchasing  Contract  Define Number Ranges (see Figure 8.21).

Release Procedure for Contracts
If you require purchase contracts to be approved, and you are not using the purchase
contract flexible workflow capabilities of SAP S/4HANA, you can still use the characteristic-
based release procedures for contracts that were available in SAP ERP. For example, if
the target value of a contract exceeds $10,000, perhaps it may have to be approved by
a manager before the contract can be processed further. The approver in this process
uses a predetermined release code to approve (release) the document. The procedure is
set up in a series of configuration steps:
1. Navigate to IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Purchasing  Contract  Release
Procedure for Contracts, as shown in Figure 8.22.
Figure 8.22 Release Procedure for Contracts
2. Create characteristics.
3. Create classes.
4. Set up the release procedure for contracts.
5. Create release group.
6. Create release code.
7. Create release indicators.
8. Create release strategies.
9. Check release strategies.
We recommend reviewing the detailed documentation in the IMG help on setting up
release procedures for contracts.
Texts for Contracts
Text types are used while creating contracts, and text maintained under each text type
is generally used to provide additional information either at the header level or item
level within the contract. For this functionality to work, text types must be defined. In
this customizing step, it’s possible to check the SAP defined standard text types and
create new text types if needed. In addition, you can define copying rules for adopting
texts from other objects, such as an RFQ, quotation, or a contract. To begin the config-
uration, follow these steps:

1. Navigate to IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Purchasing  Contract  Texts for
Contracts, as shown in Figure 8.23.
Figure 8.23 Texts for Contracts
2. Check the available text types and define your own text types for contract header
texts if needed.
3. After the text types are defined, open the Define Copying Rules for Header Texts
node, select the text type for which copying rules need to be defined, and choose

4. On the Maintain Text Linkages: Header Text Contract screen, enter the source object

the copying rule to any one of the following options:
– Text automatically adopted in target object
– User can have text adopted in target object
– Text can’t be adopted in target object
This customizing activity is similar for contract item text types.

8.5 Scheduling Agreement
8.5 Scheduling Agreement
Scheduling agreements are another form of outline purchase agreement in SAP S/4HANA.
These agreements are used to procure materials over a specified period of time following
a set schedule of delivery. The predetermined delivery schedules in the agreement indi-
cate quantities of items and dates of delivery. These delivery schedules are periodically
communicated to the supplier instead of sending purchase orders to meet the require-
ments.
Conditions for scheduling agreements can be maintained at the header level, which
applies to all the items, or at the item level, which applies only to a specific item. These
agreements have the account assignment function, which allows the buyer to allocate
costs by maintaining details of controlling objects at the item level within the docu-
ment at the time of creation.
The benefits of using scheduling agreements include the following:
 Shorten processing times and reduce the amount of paperwork required otherwise
 Delivery schedule can replace a large number of discrete purchase orders or contract
release orders
 Reduced inventory
 Possible to run manufacturing operations with the just-in-time principle
 Suppliers require shorter lead times with smaller deliveries spread over a long
period, resulting in better planning and efficient resource allocation for suppliers
 Scheduling agreement can work in conjunction with MRP, especially in repetitive
manufacturing involving large quantities
There are several different types of scheduling agreements available in SAP S/4HANA.
We will describe each type in detail. We will then describe the various apps available to
create and manage these documents. We will also describe a useful app that lets you
monitor spend and invoice history for scheduling agreement line items.
8.5.1 Scheduling Agreement Types
The different types of scheduling agreements are defined in the SAP S/4HANA system
by document types defined in customizing. The three document types that are pre-
defined in the standard system are explained in the following sections. In addition to
these three, it’s possible to define your own custom document types depending on
your business requirements. More details are provided in Section 8.6.
Scheduling Agreement with Release Document
This type of scheduling agreement is created by choosing document type LPA. In this
case, the schedule lines entered within the agreement aren’t transmitted to the sup-
plier at the time of creation of the agreement and are internal to the system. The

schedule lines maintained in this agreement can be changed at any time during the
life of the agreement, which allows some level of flexibility in scheduling procure-
ment based on changing requirements. Whenever a scheduling agreement release is
created, the information stored in the schedule lines is aggregated into time buckets,
and then transmitted to the supplier.
Two types of releases available with this type of scheduling agreement (LPA) are the
forecast delivery schedule (FRC) and the just-in-time (JIT) delivery schedule. The JIT
delivery schedule is firm within a defined time fence, and the supplier can rely on these
numbers rarely changing. The forecast delivery schedule is usually generated for time
periods further out and used for planning purposes. The release documentation gener-
ated in this process provides information about the releases transmitted to the sup-
plier over a set period, and are stored in the SAP S/4HANA system for reference.
Scheduling Agreement without Release Document
This type of scheduling agreement is created by choosing document type LP. The
scheduling lines created in this type of agreement are external and official. This means
that the scheduling lines are transmitted to the supplier as soon as they’re created.
Also, there is no release documentation associated with this agreement.
Stock Transport Scheduling Agreement
If a company is procuring materials internally from another plant on a regular basis,
it’s possible to set up a stock transport scheduling agreement by choosing document
type LU at the time of creation. SAP standard uses item category U (Stock Transfer) for
this type of agreement.

8.6.4 Maintain Release Creation Profile
A release creation profile is used to determine the period in which releases (types of

creation strategy and how backlog and immediate requirements are considered in the

8.7 Integrating with SAP Ariba Contracts
8.7 Integrating with SAP Ariba Contracts
SAP Ariba Contracts is a comprehensive contract management solution that allows an
enterprise to create and manage legal contracts with their suppliers. These contracts
can be collaboratively created in SAP Ariba, and then routed for approval in SAP Ariba.
Once the contracts are fully approved and are ready for use, they can be automatically
integrated into SAP S/4HANA for use as operational outline agreements. The steps in
this flow are detailed here:
1. Contract administrators create the contract document in SAP Ariba Contracts. The
use of contract templates or copying from existing contracts are two options for
manual creation. If integration with SAP Ariba Sourcing is available, then the con-
tract as awarded in that module can be imported and augmented in SAP Ariba Con-
tracts, thus speeding up contract creation.
2. The specific terms and conditions that apply to that contract are stipulated in the
body of the contract, along with payment terms, validity periods, and a listing of the
agreed upon items, contract quantities, and pricing that has been negotiated with
the supplier.
3. You then select the follow-on document type in the operational system. For SAP
S/4HANA, this would be either a contract or a scheduling agreement document type.
4. The completed contract is then routed for approval through an approval process
that is set up for your enterprise in SAP Ariba Contracts.
5. Once the contract approval is obtained, the contract is then released in SAP Ariba
Contracts. This triggers the integration of the approved, released contract into SAP
S/4HANA.
6. Once the outline agreement (contract or scheduling agreement) document is cre-
ated via the integration, an optional approval process flow can be optionally kicked
off in SAP S/4HANA for that document. As the document goes through the approval
process in SAP S/4HANA, this progress is reflected via status changes that are sent
back to SAP Ariba Contracts, which updates the original contract.
7. Once the operational document is fully approved in SAP S/4HANA, it can then be set
up as a valid source of supply via a source list in SAP S/4HANA for automatic source
assignment.
8. If the approved operational document is a value or quantity contract, purchase
orders can now be created with reference to the contract document in the usual
manner.
9. If the approved operational document is a scheduling agreement, then delivery
schedule lines can be generated during materials planning, and delivery schedules
can subsequently be created and transmitted to the supplier.

8.8 Summary
Contract and scheduling agreement management is a core area for procurement orga-
nizations. Without an existing agreement in place, it’s difficult to drive disciplined pric-
ing and terms. Contracts can be tied to catalog items to underpin a clear ordering
process and user experience, representing a model way to conduct corporate purchas-
ing. SAP S/4HANA updates many older transaction codes and screens with SAP Fiori
apps, but much of the setup and configuration remains the same. However, there are
now shortcuts in the form of SAP Best Practices activation, which automatically sets up
standard functionality in the system.
This chapter focused on the operational contracts and scheduling agreements. Organi-
zations can also use SAP S/4HANA to manage their legal contract documents as well.
The next chapter will focus on the SAP offerings for enterprise contract management
and assembly.
